title: Checkpoint: The Sun’s Domain
objective: After this level you can describe the Sun and everything it influences, from its core to the Oort Cloud.
summary: The solar wind blows a bubble, the heliosphere, around the planets. Voyager 1 crossed its edge in 2012.

cards.headline: Chapter 6 finale. Where does the solar system actually end?
cards.body: It depends on what you measure. The Kuiper Belt keeps going past Neptune, the solar wind blows farther still, and the Sun's gravity reaches farthest of all.

cards.headline: The Sun's bubble
cards.body: Remember the solar wind from Level 58? It blows a vast bubble around the Sun and planets called the heliosphere. Its outer edge, the heliopause, is where the solar wind gives way to interstellar space. Voyager 1 crossed it in 2012. By that measure, our most distant spacecraft has left home.

cards.headline: But gravity reaches farther
cards.body: By another measure, it's still in the front yard. The Sun's gravity holds on far beyond the heliosphere, out to the Oort Cloud, the outermost part of the solar system, which may reach 100,000 AU. Voyager 1 won't reach even its inner edge for about 300 years. Asteroid belt, Kuiper Belt, Oort Cloud: the Sun's domain runs much farther than its planets.

options.label: The bubble the solar wind blows around the Sun and planets
The Sun’s visible surface layer
The ring of icy bodies beyond Neptune
The path of the Sun across the sky

questions.explanation: The heliosphere is the vast bubble of solar wind surrounding the solar system.

questions.prompt: Which layer of the Sun is over a million degrees Celsius?

options.label: The photosphere
The convective zone
The corona
The chromosphere
options.rationale: The corona, above it, is far hotter.

questions.explanation: The corona, the Sun’s outer atmosphere, is over 1 million °C.

questions.prompt: Voyager 1 has left the heliosphere. Has it left the solar system?

options.label: Yes, the heliopause is the end of everything
options.rationale: The Sun’s gravity reaches much farther.

options.label: Yes, it passed the Oort Cloud years ago
options.rationale: It won’t reach the Oort Cloud for ~300 years.

options.label: Not by the Sun’s gravity: the Oort Cloud lies far beyond
No, it is still inside the asteroid belt

questions.explanation: Voyager 1 has entered interstellar space, but the Sun’s gravity still rules out to the Oort Cloud, which it won’t reach for centuries.

questions.prompt: What do auroras on Earth have to do with the Sun?

options.label: They are reflected sunlight from polar ice
They are the Sun’s corona seen at night
options.rationale: The corona is only visible near the Sun.

options.label: They are caused by meteors burning up
options.rationale: Meteors are streaks, not glowing curtains.

options.label: Solar particles striking the upper air near the poles

questions.explanation: Charged particles from the Sun, steered by Earth’s magnetic field, make the air near the poles glow.

questions.prompt: Chapter 6 recap: which list goes from nearest to farthest from the Sun?

options.label: Oort Cloud → Kuiper Belt → asteroid belt
Asteroid belt → Kuiper Belt → Oort Cloud
Kuiper Belt → asteroid belt → Oort Cloud
options.rationale: The asteroid belt is inside Jupiter’s orbit.

options.label: Asteroid belt → Oort Cloud → Kuiper Belt
options.rationale: The Oort Cloud is the most distant.

questions.explanation: The asteroid belt lies between Mars and Jupiter, the Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune, and the Oort Cloud far beyond both.
